subject: Latency & throughput follow-up — SLO alignment and cost levers
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: María González <maria.gonzalez@avatest.com>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 17 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Latency & throughput follow-up — SLO alignment and cost levers

Hi María —

Thanks again for the intro call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum:

Key requirements you shared
- Target p95 latency: 150 ms for interactive streaming responses (chat-like UI)
- Sustained throughput: ~120 requests/sec with 30–50 concurrent sessions (bursty peaks up to 140 req/s)
- Maximum tail concurrency: ~50 concurrent long-running streams
- Average response length: 30–80 tokens, occasional long-form generation up to 600 tokens
- Data residency: EU-only; retention policy requires logs to be purged after 90 days

Budget/constraints you mentioned
- Goal: keep unit inference cost <= $X per 1M tokens (you asked us to provide concrete scenarios)
- Security: SOC 2 evidence required; procurement will share NDA and baseline questionnaire

Immediate proposal (short list)
1) Quick benchmark: run a 2-hour micro-benchmark against a dedicated pool to validate p95 and throughput. Redwood will provide a test harness and a sample workload that mirrors your token distribution.
2) Cost/perf levers to evaluate during the benchmark:
   - Continuous batching with latency caps (reduces per-token cost while meeting p95)
   - Prefix/KV caching for repeated prompts (chat history reuse)
   - Model variants + quantization profiles: 7B int8 for sub-second tails, 13B int4 for higher quality when latency budget allows
   - Streaming chunk size tuning to trade off head latency vs total time-to-first-token
3) Next steps: can you confirm target concurrency for the benchmark and who from security should join? I propose a 60–90 minute technical run-through next week.

I've attached a rough SLO impact CSV and our dataplane diagram for context. If you want, Sergio can outline a recommended config for Dedicated capacity to hit 150 ms p95 while minimizing cost.

Thanks — I’ll follow up with a short mutual-action plan and a couple of calendar options.

Best,
Rishi
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
https://redwood.com

Attachments: SLO-impact-estimates.csv, redwood-dataplane-arch.png
From: María González <maria.gonzalez@avatest.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Cc: security@avatest.com, procurement@avatest.com
Date: Mon, 17 Feb 2026 14:03:00 +00:00
Subject: Re: Latency & throughput follow-up — SLO alignment and cost levers

Hi Rishi —

Appreciate the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side:
- Concurrency: planning for 30 concurrent active sessions initially; architecture must support burst to 140 req/s across our EU region during marketing spikes.
- Streaming behavior: we do need token-by-token streaming to our frontend; head latency < 200 ms is a hard requirement for desktop users.
- Caching: we cannot persist user prompts to shared caches outside the customer's tenancy due to retention policy; per-request KV/caching strategies are acceptable if they live in our VPC or are ephemeral.
- Security: adding our InfoSec contact on cc (security@avatest.com). Procurement will send NDA shortly (attached).

Can Sergio and Marissa provide a cost scenario for 1M tokens at the recommended quantization profiles and an estimate for Dedicated vs Hosted for the benchmark?

Available next week for the micro-benchmark on Tuesday or Wednesday afternoon CET.

Thanks,
María
Head of Product, AvaTest

Attachment: NDA_signed.pdf
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
To: María González <maria.gonzalez@avatest.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 17 Feb 2026 15:10:00 +00:00
Subject: Re: Latency & throughput follow-up — SLO alignment and cost levers

Hi María —

Thanks — a few technical notes ahead of the benchmark to set expectations and recommended configs: 

1) Streaming/head latency: to hit p95 ~150 ms we recommend
   - Continuous batching with a headroom latency cap of 60–80 ms on the serving side (this keeps queuing short).
   - Small streaming chunk sizes for first-chunk under 80 ms, then larger chunks for throughput.

2) Concurrency/throughput: with Dedicated GPU pools we can reliably sustain 120–140 req/s at the target token sizes if you provision pools sized for your peak concurrency (we'll size based on the 30 active sessions and the 140 req/s burst profile).

3) Caching/retention constraints: given your retention rules, we'll run KV/prefix caching in a tenant-scoped ephemeral store inside your VPC for the POC so nothing leaves your tenancy. That preserves the cost/perf benefit while satisfying compliance.

4) Quantization & model variant strategy
   - Baseline quality: redwood-alpha-13B quantized to int4 — best quality with mid cost. Expect ~30–45% cost reduction vs FP16 with careful kernel selection.
   - Low-cost fallback: redwood-alpha-7B int8 — lower token cost and faster latency for short responses. Configure automatic routing for low-latency paths during peaks.

5) Estimated unit costs (back-of-envelope for benchmark traffic)
   - 13B int4: ~ $Y / 1M tokens
   - 7B int8: ~ $Z / 1M tokens (roughly 40–60% of 13B int4 cost depending on batching)

Next actions I can take this week:
- Provide a Detailed Benchmark Plan (test script + expected metrics)
- Create two config profiles (Dedicated sizing + Hosted fallback) for you to review

Can we lock Tuesday 15:00 CET for the bench kickoff? I’ll include the benchmark harness and a simple Prometheus/Grafana view for p95, p99, TPS, and CPU/GPU utilization.

— Sergio
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: María González <maria.gonzalez@avatest.com>

Sergio —

Tuesday 15:00 CET works for us. Please add our InfoSec engineer (security@avatest.com) to any security-specific artifacts. Procurement will follow up with contract contacts for Dedicated pricing.

We also need a short checklist for our infra team so they can open the necessary VPC peering, IAM roles, and KMS access for the POC. Could you include that in the benchmark plan?

Thanks,
María
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>

Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, security@avatest.com, procurement@avatest.com
Date: Mon, 17 Feb 2026 16:38:00 +00:00
Subject: Re: Latency & throughput follow-up — SLO alignment and cost levers

Perfect — locked in Tuesday 15:00 CET for the POC kickoff.

I’ve uploaded a short mutual-action plan and the infra checklist to the linked Drive folder (see related links). High-level checklist items we’ll send in the benchmark plan:
- VPC peering / private link config (EU region)
- IAM role with least-privilege for benchmark harness and ephemeral KV store
- KMS key policy for encryption-in-transit and at-rest for ephemeral caches
- Network egress rules and retention settings to ensure 90-day purge

Sergio will share the benchmark script and cost scenarios by EOD tomorrow; Marissa will include the onboarding steps for Dedicated pools if you want to run under reserved capacity.

If procurement wants a Dedicated vs Hosted price comparison aside from the rough estimates, I can get a formal quote ready ahead of the call.

Cheers,
Rishi
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
